mainEntity.name: What is a Web3 PR campaign and what does it cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Web3 PR campaign is the full sequence from positioning thesis to post-launch sentiment for a single news moment in crypto: a mainnet launch, a funding round, an exchange listing, a token generation event, a major protocol upgrade, or a category-defining op-ed cycle. The work covers narrative architecture, journalist mapping to the right beats at Forbes, CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, Decrypt, The Block and Blockworks, embargo coordination across multiple outlets and regions, KOL wave timing, crisis-comms readiness for depegs or governance incidents, and weekly sentiment and AI-citation reporting. A fractional senior operator runs the whole sequence directly with the founder, in place of a multi-person agency account team.

mainEntity.name: When should a Web3 founder hire a PR consultant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Six to twelve weeks before any planned public moment. That covers mainnet launch, token generation event, exchange listing, funding announcement, major protocol upgrade, and the first conference where the founder needs a real stage. Hiring inside three weeks of the moment still works for a tight sprint but cuts off the highest-leverage work: positioning, journalist relationship build, embargo prep, and KOL coordination. Hiring after the moment is over wastes most of the news cycle and forces a slower category-narrative build.

mainEntity.name: How much does a Web3 PR campaign cost in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: A fractional Web3 PR retainer in 2026 runs $5,000 to $12,000 per month. A mainnet, product or funding launch sprint over four to eight weeks runs $15,000 to $40,000, scoped by the size of the moment and the number of regions in play. Traditional Web3 PR agency retainers are commonly $15,000 to $30,000 per month because that funds a multi-person account team. The fractional model removes the account-team layer: one senior operator works directly with the founder. Project-based pricing is usually the better fit for token launches and exchange listings where two to four weeks of concentrated work matters more than a year-long retainer.

mainEntity.name: What outlets does a Web3 PR campaign target?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tier-1 crypto-native: CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, The Block, Decrypt, Blockworks, The Defiant. Tier-1 mainstream: Forbes, Bloomberg, Wall Street Journal, Reuters where the story has a funding or regulation angle. Vertical and regional: Bitcoin Magazine, NFTNow, CryptoSlate, CryptoNews, CryptoPotato, Yahoo Finance, Benzinga, plus BloomingBit in Korea, CryptoTimes JP and CoinPost in Japan, ChainCatcher and Jinse in China, Inc42 and YourStory in India, and e27 across Southeast Asia. The named beat reporter at each outlet matters more than the masthead — a real Web3 PR program is built around journalists, not press lists.

mainEntity.name: Why does AI search visibility matter for a Web3 PR campaign in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: Crypto buyers, exchange business-development teams, and institutional allocators now research projects through ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Google AI Overviews before any sales or partnership call. When a buyer asks an AI engine 'best L1s for real-world assets' or 'top DePIN projects 2026', the answer is assembled from earned editorial coverage, analyst-style write-ups, and structured author-attributed content, not from the project's own marketing pages. Independent 2026 research consistently finds earned coverage accounts for the large majority of links AI engines cite, while press releases account for roughly one percent. Every Web3 PR campaign is structured to produce the earned, named, schema-eligible content AI engines retrieve.

mainEntity.name: How is a fractional Web3 PR consultant different from a crypto PR agency?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three differences. One: the operator is in the room. A fractional consultant works directly with the founder, CMO and head of comms with no account-team layer routing every decision through a junior. Two: scope follows the news, not the retainer. A fractional engagement is sized to the moments ahead (mainnet, TGE, raise, listing) instead of a fixed monthly menu of deliverables. Three: cost is roughly half. A senior fractional retainer at $5K to $12K per month replaces a $15K to $30K per month agency retainer for the same senior-led scope, because the model removes the AE, account director and junior layer. Agencies still win for projects that genuinely need a multi-region, multi-language production team running in parallel. Most pre-Series B Web3 startups do not.

mainEntity.name: How does a Web3 PR campaign run in Korea in 2026 (FSC, DABA, exchange listings, KBW)?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Korea-anchored Web3 PR campaign in 2026 pivots on three live regulatory beats and one event cycle. Press copy carries the FSC five-minute reconciliation and zero-threshold Travel Rule note, the Digital Asset Basic Act (DABA) status line, and the KRW-stablecoin route through licensed banks where applicable. Tier-1 placements are BloomingBit, TokenPost, BlockMedia, Coinness and CoinReaders. Exchange-listing answer (Upbit, Bithumb, Coinone, Korbit, Gopax) is the first question every Korean trade reporter asks, so the press kit leads with it. Korean Telegram and Naver KOL waves are timed to embargo lift at 10 AM KST. Korea Blockchain Week 2026 (September 22 to 28, Impact at COEX) is the highest-leverage press cycle of the year. Naver and Kakao AI surfaces preferentially cite Korean-original editorial; translated Western press kits are not enough.

mainEntity.name: How does a Web3 PR campaign run in Japan in 2026 (FSA, FIEA, NISA spot ETF, WebX)?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Japan-anchored Web3 PR campaign in 2026 runs against the April 2026 Cabinet-approved FIEA reclassification of 105 crypto assets including BTC and ETH as financial instruments, the June 1 2026 Payment Services Act amendments that opened the foreign trust-type stablecoin route, the 20% flat capital-gains tax reform replacing the progressive 55% rate, and the spot BTC and ETH ETF NISA Growth-tier pipeline through SBI and Nomura. Outlets are CoinPost, CoinDesk Japan, Cointelegraph Japan, CryptoTimes JP, Iolite, Nikkei and Nikkei Cross Tech. Japanese press wants a partner-name credibility anchor and a clean-data table, not a hero-narrative pitch. WebX 2026 (July 13 to 14, The Prince Park Tower Tokyo, 13,160 attendees from 88 countries) is the press cycle anchor. note.com is the highest-leverage AI-search citation unlock per dollar; LINE Open Chat is the closed-community primary hub.

mainEntity.name: How does a Web3 PR campaign run in Singapore in 2026 (MAS, Project Guardian, Token2049)?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Singapore-anchored Web3 PR campaign in 2026 leads with MAS licensing status (DPT licence, exemption status, or Project Guardian participation) as the credibility frame. The Project Guardian tokenization workstreams are the institutional narrative bridge to BlackRock, JPMorgan, DBS, Citi, HSBC and Standard Chartered. Token2049 Singapore (October, Marina Bay Sands, 20,000-plus attendees) is the regional press cycle anchor. Outlets are e27, Tech in Asia, DealStreetAsia, Token2049 newsroom, plus regional crypto desks. A generic raise without a Singapore anchor reads as a press blip. Every Singapore announcement carries three lines: MAS status, Singapore-as-regional-headquarters framing for tax and corporate-structure clarity, and the named local-partner anchor that ties the announcement to the Singapore ecosystem rather than treating Singapore as a generic Asia stop.

mainEntity.name: How does a Web3 PR campaign run in Dubai and MENA in 2026 (VARA, ADGM, RAK DAO, Token2049 Dubai)?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Dubai and MENA Web3 PR campaign in 2026 is anchored on three regulators (VARA in Dubai, ADGM's FSRA in Abu Dhabi, RAK DAO in Ras Al Khaimah), the May 2026 Token2049 Dubai press cycle, and the regional category position MANTRA's $11M raise established (Abu Dhabi-based lead investor as a Middle East RWA story). Outlets are Arabian Business, Gulf News, The National and Cointelegraph Arabic, plus regional re-reports through CryptoPotato and Decrypt MENA. MENA press wants a UAE or Saudi regulatory tie-in, a named local partner and a Token2049 Dubai stage moment. Press copy carries a per-jurisdiction note: VARA for Dubai-licensed operations, FSRA for ADGM-domiciled vehicles, RAK DAO for DAO-structured tokenized treasuries. The Saudi PIF and Mubadala lines decide what stage is even available.

mainEntity.name: How does a Web3 PR campaign run in India in 2026 (SEBI, MeitY, Inc42, ETHIndia)?

acceptedAnswer.text: An India-anchored Web3 PR campaign in 2026 runs three press tracks in parallel plus the ETHIndia December press cycle. Mainstream business is Economic Times, Business Today, Forbes India and Mint. Startup-and-VC is Inc42, YourStory and Moneycontrol. Crypto-native is CoinGape, NewsBTC India and HackerNoon for founder interviews. Indian press wants founder country of origin, lead-investor name and SEBI-and-MeitY-adjacent regulatory framing — a Western-style raise pitch without the regulatory acknowledgement gets re-reported with the gap noted. The Bullieverse $4M seed was launched as an Economic Times exclusive then run on two parallel tracks (mainstream Indian business plus crypto-native), each with its own framing of the same fact sheet. Indian retail audiences route through X, YouTube and Telegram tri-platform creators, not a single channel.
